# Dropdown

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

overlays · tier 1 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a short list of actions or links behind one button.
Anything that is not a row (a field, a paragraph) goes in a Popover.

```ts
import {
  DropdownGroup, DropdownGroupLabel, DropdownItem, DropdownLinkItem, DropdownMenu, DropdownPopup, DropdownRoot,
  DropdownSeparator, DropdownTrigger,
} from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
<DropdownRoot>
  <DropdownTrigger render={<Button variant="outline">Actions</Button>} />
  <DropdownPopup>
    <DropdownItem shortcut="Ctrl P">Profile</DropdownItem>
    <DropdownItem disabled>Rename</DropdownItem>
    <DropdownSeparator />
    <DropdownItem tone="danger">Delete</DropdownItem>
  </DropdownPopup>
</DropdownRoot>
```

- **Parts.** Flat names and no bare `Dropdown`: `DropdownRoot`, `DropdownTrigger`,
  `DropdownPopup`, `DropdownItem`, `DropdownLinkItem`, `DropdownGroup`,
  `DropdownGroupLabel`, `DropdownSeparator`. Each passes the rest of its props to the
  element it draws. `DropdownRoot` draws none.
- **A row.** `icon` before the label, `shortcut` after it. A label too long for the menu
  ends in an ellipsis, and one past 100 characters is cut.
- **A row with an icon alone.** It needs `aria-label`, and the types ask for it. The icon
  is hidden from a screen reader, so it is never the name.
- **`tone="danger"`.** It only colours the row. A reader who cannot see red, and anyone
  under forced colours, sees a row like the others: write what it does in the label
  ("Delete project"), add an icon, and put a `DropdownSeparator` above it.
- **A disabled row.** Dimmed. The arrow keys still stop on it and it is announced as
  unavailable; Enter, Space and a press do nothing.
- **Placement.** `placement` on `DropdownPopup`: twelve values, `bottom-start` by default.
  `start` and `end` are the reading sides, so they swap in Arabic. Never `left` or `right`.
- **At an edge.** It opens on the other side when its own has no room, lines up the other
  edge when that one has none, and stays 8 px inside the screen.
- **Width.** As wide as its longest row: 192 px at least, 320 px at most, never wider than
  the screen. For another cap, pass a class: `className="max-w-96"`.
- **A long menu.** It shows about seven rows (`--tc-list-rows`), cuts the last one so it is
  plain there are more, and scrolls inside itself. The page does not move. While it
  scrolls it is a tab stop, so one a press opened is still reached. You write no `tabIndex`.
- **Not a collection.** Every row is mounted. Base UI's Menu has no windowing, and its
  arrow keys and type-ahead reach mounted rows only. Keep a menu to tens of rows.
- **Keys.** On the trigger: Enter, Space and ArrowDown open it on the first row, ArrowUp
  on the last. In the menu: the arrows move and loop, Home and End jump, a letter goes to
  the row that starts with it, Enter and Space run the row, Escape closes it.
- **Space after a letter.** Right after you typed a letter, Space is part of the search
  ("zone 4"), as in a native menu. It runs the row again after a short pause.
- **Tab.** It closes the menu and goes on to the next control of the page. Shift+Tab closes
  it and returns to the trigger.
- **Closing.** A press on a row, Escape, or a press outside. Focus returns to the trigger.
- **Escape.** It closes one thing: a tooltip open on a row first, then the menu, then the
  dialog around it.
- **Labels.** `render={<Button>Actions</Button>}`, or `render={<Button />}` with `Actions`
  as children. On a server page only the first keeps the ellipsis of a long label.
- **Arabic inside an English page.** The menu takes its direction and its language from
  the nearest `TopClassProvider`. With no provider it takes those of the page.

### From data

```tsx
<DropdownMenu
  trigger={<Button variant="outline">Account</Button>}
  title="Account"
  link={<Link href="" />}
  items={[
    { id: 'profile', label: 'Profile', shortcut: 'Ctrl P', href: '/profile' },
    { id: 'settings', label: 'Settings', href: '/settings' },
    { id: 'signout', label: 'Sign out', tone: 'danger', separatorBefore: true, action: signOut },
  ]}
/>
```

- **`title`.** It names the group the rows are in, and is shown above them.
- **An item is one of three kinds.** `href` is a link. `action` is a Server Action: a
  press calls it with an empty `FormData`, inside a transition, so what it throws reaches
  your error boundary. `onSelect` is a plain function.
- **`link`.** Every `href` row is cloned from it, with its own `href`. Pass the `Link` of
  your framework, or the page reloads on every row. With no `link` a row is a plain `<a>`.
- **`icon`.** An element: `icon: <Icon name="user" />` on a server page, `<Svg icon={user} />`
  in a client file.
- **`disabled`.** A disabled `href` item is a row with no `href`, not a link.
- **From a server page.** `href`, `action`, `link`, `trigger` and `icon` cross to the
  browser. `onSelect` and `onOpenChange` are plain functions and do not: they need a
  `'use client'` file.

### Links

```tsx
<DropdownRoot>
  <DropdownTrigger render={<Button variant="outline">Help</Button>} />
  <DropdownPopup>
    <DropdownLinkItem href="/docs">Documentation</DropdownLinkItem>
    <DropdownLinkItem render={<Link href="/support" />}>Contact support</DropdownLinkItem>
  </DropdownPopup>
</DropdownRoot>
```

- **A real anchor.** Open in a new tab and middle-click work. A press closes the menu.
- **`render`.** For one row as the `Link` of your framework. Write the `href` on that
  element: its own props win.
- **No `disabled`.** Base UI's link item has none. Render a `DropdownItem disabled` instead.

### What Base UI gives

| Prop | On | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | `DropdownRoot` | Open state, yours or its own. |
| `modal` | `DropdownRoot` | Whether the page behind is blocked. See below. |
| `loopFocus` | `DropdownRoot` | `false` stops the arrows at both ends. |
| `highlightItemOnHover` | `DropdownRoot` | `false` leaves the highlight to the keyboard. |
| `openOnHover`, `delay`, `closeDelay` | `DropdownTrigger` | The pointer opens it too. Milliseconds, 0 to 10000; left out: 100 and 0. |
| `closeOnClick` | `DropdownItem`, `DropdownLinkItem` | `false` keeps the menu open after the row ran. |
| `label` | `DropdownItem`, `DropdownLinkItem` | The text type-ahead matches, when it is not the row's own. |
| `finalFocus` | `DropdownPopup` | Where focus goes on close. |
| `container`, `keepMounted` | `DropdownPopup` | Where it mounts, and whether it stays mounted while closed. |
| `nativeButton` | `DropdownTrigger` | `false` when `render` is not a button. |

- **`modal` (the default).** The page behind does not scroll and takes no press: a press
  outside only closes the menu. Nothing dims it, and a screen reader can still read it.
- **`modal={false}`.** The page scrolls and takes presses. The menu follows its trigger,
  and hides while the trigger is scrolled out of view.
- **`modal` on a phone.** A tap outside still only closes it, but the page scrolls.
- **A menu the pointer opened** (`openOnHover`) is never modal.

### Not built

Checkbox items, radio items and submenus (all three are drawn), `size` (one row height),
a visible arrow, icons by name (`icon` is an element), windowing, `sideOffset` as a prop,
and a trigger outside its `DropdownRoot` (Base UI's `handle`).

## Import

```tsx
import { Dropdown } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The trigger and the popup. With no trigger, hold `open` in a client file. |
| `closeDelay` | no | `number`, min 0, max 10000 | `0` | DropdownTrigger, with openOnHover: milliseconds it stays open after the pointer leaves, clamped. |
| `delay` | no | `number`, min 0, max 10000 | `100` | DropdownTrigger, with openOnHover: milliseconds of hover before it opens, clamped. |
| `placement` | no | `top` \| `top-start` \| `top-end` \| `bottom` \| `bottom-start` \| `bottom-end` \| `start` \| `start-top` \| `start-bottom` \| `end` \| `end-top` \| `end-bottom` | `"bottom-start"` | DropdownPopup, DropdownMenu: the side and alignment it opens at; start and end mirror in Arabic. |
| `tone` | no | `neutral` \| `danger` | `"neutral"` | DropdownItem, DropdownLinkItem: danger colours a destructive row; its label still has to say so. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
